summary: Inheritance makes a new class that starts with all the fields and methods of an existing class. You add new methods or override old ones in the subclass.
notes: class HonorsStudent extends Student names the one parent class. Java allows only one class after extends.
super(name, scores); must be the first statement in the subclass constructor.
super.describe() calls the parent's version of a method you have overridden.
pitfall: Leaving out super(name, scores); fails to compile with "constructor Student in class Student cannot be applied to given types", because Java tries to call a Student() constructor that does not exist.
